summary: Internal enablement: rapid-fire demo practice with roleplay from Nimbus Analytics. Focus on messaging pivots for latency vs cost, hosted vs dedicated, and SOC2/KMS security talking points. Practiced three short scenarios (support triage, embedding search, private deployment ask). Identified common objections and agreed next steps to share assets and a sandbox link.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-19 14:00 PDT | Duration ~75m | Recording: Fireflies
Attendees: Jordan (AE), Aisha (SE), Liam (Principal SE), Maya (Enablement) - Redwood; Sofia (Sr PM), Ethan (ML Eng), Priya (Eng Mgr) - Nimbus Analytics

00:00 Jordan: Alright team, thanks for carving time. This is the practical demo lab, rapid-fire, so we do short 4-6 minute scenarios with live roleplay. We want the field to leave with two things: one, a crisp arc for the demo, and two, a fallback for the stickier security asks.
00:24 Aisha: Quick note, I'm going to try both hosted and dedicated variants in the same flow so we can show routing and fallback. Audio might glitch when I flip models because of local clips, so bear with me.
00:34 Liam: Perfect. Maya, do we have the slide with the demo arc?
00:38 Maya: Yep I just posted it in the chat — it's the redwood-rapid-fire deck. Link: /assets/rapid-fire-deck (demoers, use the last two slides for objection handling)
00:49 Jordan: Cool. Scenario 1: Support triage. Customer prompt comes in, we show retrieval via embeddings + short generative summary. Aisha, you're on. Sofia you'll roleplay the PM complaining about hallucinations. Ready?
01:02 Aisha: Ready. Starting demo — "Hey support, user says invoice number 9932 didn't charge" — I'm going to call embeddings, show similarity search, then generate a 2-sentence summary.
01:22 [sound of keyboard clatter]
01:26 Ethan: Quick interruption, in real PoCs our vector DB is hosted separately. Make sure to note how Redwood returns structured (json) vs raw text, customers care about schema.
01:37 Aisha: Good call. I'm calling the /generate with format: {"response_format":"json","fields":["summary","confidence"]} — note: the demo uses a quirky paraphrase of Redwood's api, sometimes transcription shows that as "Redwood infer" in notes.
01:55 Sofia (roleplay): The summary looks good, but I saw the model invent a policy clause — that's a hallucination. How do you prevent that in production?
02:05 Aisha: Two levers — first, retrieval quality: use high-k + rerank and a stricter similarity threshold. Second, guardrails: we prefer structured output + deterministic post-filtering. Mention our Evaluate + rollback hooks in console.
02:23 Jordan: Add the cost tradeoff — higher k and reranking increases tokens and latency; call out the Optimize recommendations for batching/caching to offset.
02:30 Sofia: So if I bump k from 5 to 12 what's the cost delta?
02:33 Liam: Very roughly, linear-ish on tokens returned from the DB + generation tokens. For short synopses it's small, for long context retrieval it adds. We have a cost calculator (link shared) — show that during pricing conversations.
02:50 Aisha: End of scenario 1. Quick debrief: we used hosted model with caching; we called out fallback to a quantized dedicated endpoint if latency spikes.
03:05 Jordan: Scenario 2: Realtime chat with private data — customer asks for on-prem or VPC. Priya, you'll press on data residency and KMS.
03:15 Priya (roleplay): Our compliance team says we need customer-managed keys and audit logs. Also, do you do air-gapped installs?
03:23 Aisha: We have Redwood Private: VPC + on-prem options. For KMS we integrate with AWS KMS and support customer-provided keys; audit logs are exported to CloudWatch/Splunk. Air-gapped on-prem packages are available for enterprise deals.
03:40 Priya: Any SOC2 or ISO certs?
03:44 Liam: Yes, SOC 2 Type II in progress and we have ISO plans; mention we can provide a security packet and redacted audit.
03:52 [murmur: "packet, packet"]
03:55 Jordan: Practice the line: "We map to your compliance controls and can provide artifact-level evidence; for high-assurance workloads we recommend Private with customer KMS and audit export."
04:10 Aisha: Demo detail: show the console toggle for deploying to Dedicated vs Private. I'm switching to the console view — note: the UI animates, might stutter on the recording.
04:28 Ethan: Small nit, customers will ask about performance on Private — especially KV cache behavior. How do we explain model variants and quantization impact?
04:36 Liam: Two parts: quality and latency. On Private we recommend A/B testing model quantization profiles with short-run experiments via Redwood Optimize. Pull out the Optimize panel during the demo and show the recommendation engine.
04:49 Jordan: Okay, scenario 3 — embedding search at scale for semantic search. We want to show vector chunking, prefix caching, and cost per query. Sofia, you escalate latency concerns.
05:02 Sofia: When we index 20M docs, latency is non-linear and our infra team freaks out. How do you scale?
05:11 Aisha: We use sharding at the vector-db layer, plus prefix/KV cache to cache hot keys. For inference we do continuous batching to keep GPU utilization high while preserving tail latency SLOs.
05:25 Jordan: Call out smart routing: route low-cost queries to lower-tier models and urgent queries to high-priority dedicated pools.
05:32 Sofia: Competitors like OpenAI or Anthropic claim they do the same — what's Redwood's differentiator?
05:38 Liam: The differentiator is the serving runtime and telemetry: token-level cost breakdown, per-route trace, and auto-fallback. Show the console trace for a slow request and the auto-fallback to a quantized copy.
05:53 [pause, typing sound]
05:56 Maya: Quick coaching note for the field: when competitor claims come up, pivot to specifics — ask "what's your SLO and budget" then map features to those constraints rather than high-level platform claims.
06:12 Jordan: Good. Now we're going to rapid-fire objections — each demoee gets 90 seconds to handle the objection then switch. Objection 1: "Your hosted tokens are expensive compared to Anthropic." Aisha?
06:25 Aisha: Acknowledge: "We hear that a lot; price per token varies by model and context length." Then provide the play: show our Optimize suggestions (quantize + batch) and dedicated reserved capacity pricing — and propose a pilot to measure unit economics on their workload.
06:44 Sofia (roleplay): They also want to see latency 95th percentile under load.
06:49 Jordan: Show a recent benchmark (we have one for a 2k sequence on A100). But don't recite raw numbers; instead show the trace and the specific knobs for latency (batch size, sequence truncation, kernel selection).
07:06 Ethan: During PX/PoC, customers will want to run against their prompt set. Remind the team to propose a short benchmark — 10-20 prompts that represent tails.
07:18 Aisha: End objection 1. Objection 2: "We already embedded with Vertex AI and don't want vendor lock-in." Liam?
07:27 Liam: Answer: "We offer model-level abstraction and exportable artifacts. You can pin model versions and export caches. For long-term portability, Redwood supports model artifacts that you can take to other runtimes." Keep it short and mention the migration playbook.
07:44 Sofia: Follow-up: Does Redwood support multi-cloud deployments?
07:48 Aisha: Yes — Private can be deployed in customer VPCs across clouds or on-prem, and Dedicated has region-aware clusters.
07:55 [crosstalk]
08:00 Jordan: Coaching tip: don't promise everything. Use "we recommend" language and offer the security packet.
08:05 Maya: We're going to run a live 5-minute micro-demo on the CLI: Aisha will show a fast generation call and then simulate a spike and show the fallback to dedicated.
08:14 Aisha: Executing now — calling redwood inference generate --model redwood-compact --max-tokens 120 --stream. I'm going to simulate a latency spike by switching to a heavy prompt and then trigger the rollback.
08:33 [beep]
08:36 Ethan: Uh I think the demo stubbed the wrong model name; earlier transcriptions sometimes log it as "redwood-compact" or "rwd-compact" — just note to say the model name aloud.
08:44 Aisha: Good catch. I said it aloud: redwood-compact. Generation returned quickly, streaming enabled. Now I'm toggling the load generator — see the console auto-failure and fallback to dedicated-quantized.
08:58 Sofia (roleplay): That fallback is cool. How deterministic is it? Will my requests route differently?
09:05 Liam: Routing is policy-driven: you can set per-route SLOs and routing rules; deterministic in that the policy is evaluated per request and we log the decision in tracing so you can audit.
09:18 Jordan: Ok, end of live sections. Quick meta-debrief: notes on pedagogy — 1) keep each demo under 6 minutes; 2) always start with the customer's constraint; 3) close with a clear next step (pilot/benchmark/pricing).
09:35 Maya: For the recording, I'm going to clip three moments: host fallback, KMS toggle, and cost vs latency slide. Anyone object?
09:42 Aisha: No objections.
09:44 [short pause]
09:50 Jordan: Open floor: what tripped people up? Ethan?
09:53 Ethan: A couple of things — when you mention KV cache, customers often hear it as "key value cache" and assume it's in their DB. Need to clarify it's ephemeral inference-side caching with optional persistence. Also, quantization: avoid saying "lossless" — it's lossy with measurable tradeoffs.
10:12 Sofia: On the messaging side, we want a single sentence to justify Redwood vs big cloud: "Redwood gives predictable unit economics and unified operations across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments." Can we make that pithier?
10:24 Jordan: Try: "Redwood makes inference predictable and portable — fast in hosted, repeatable in dedicated, private when required." It's rough but workable.
10:33 Maya: We'll iterate in the deck.
10:36 Liam: Coaching micro-tip: if a customer mentions "we need SOC2 now" rather than "in progress", ask for scope and timeline then offer the security packet and a technical workshop for their security team. That reduces friction.
10:50 Aisha: Last exercise: lightning demo — each Redwood attendee does a 90-second pitch + demo hook. Jordan first.
10:59 Jordan: 90 seconds: Problem statement, Redwood one-liner, 30-second demo ask, and specific next step. 
11:36 Aisha: (does demo) Quick show of CLI call, mention embeddings, mention Optimize and cost savings.
12:10 Liam: (does demo) Focus on telemetry and traceability; show console trace UI and how to read token breakdowns.
12:45 Maya: (does demo) Mention enablement assets and handoff playbook.
13:05 Sofia: Feedback from roleplay — very practical, liked the cost calculator mention. A suggestion: include a slide that compares expected token costs for 3 canonical workloads (chat, search, summarization).
13:28 Jordan: We'll add that. Any closing asks from Nimbus?
13:33 Sofia: We'd like the sandbox link and a two-week pilot outline. Also the security packet.
13:40 Jordan: Noted — add to next steps.
13:42 Priya: Also, can you run a 30-minute security deep dive with our compliance lead next week?
13:46 Liam: Yes, I'll join. Suggest Thursday 2025-08-28 — Jordan will confirm.
13:55 Jordan: Great. Final wrap: we'll publish the clips, circulate the deck + scripts, and confirm the pilot kickoff. Thanks all.
14:04 [meeting ends, recording stops]
